title: Hurston-1 is an open text-to-speech model aimed at the phone line
friendlyTitle: An open voice model is built for the phone line, not the studio demo
summary: Destined AI has released Hurston-1, an Apache-2.0 fine-tune of Maya1 that speaks Southern American English and several African Englishes from a plain description of gender, age, accent, style, and pace. A phone mode filters the audio to the telephone band and emits 8 kHz G.711, the format a Twilio-style call expects. It does not clone a person. Each call is a new voice that fits the description, and the voice can change between chunks of a long script. Hugging Face requires you to accept the model conditions before download.
friendlySummary: Destined AI has released Hurston-1, an open fine-tune of an existing speech model. You describe the voice in plain words: gender, age, accent, style, and pace. It covers Southern American English and several African Englishes. A phone mode cuts the audio to what a phone line carries and saves it in the format a call system such as Twilio expects. It does not copy a real person. Each request is a new voice that fits the description, and a long script can change voice between chunks. Hugging Face asks you to accept the model conditions before you can download it.
whyItMatters: Most voice demos are studio audio, then the real call is a phone line. If you are testing a voice agent, an IVR, or a speech recogniser, this is a way to generate the same line in accents those systems often flatten, including the narrowband version a caller would hear. Destined's own listening test preferred it over the base model 78 percent of the time across 54 comparisons. Names and numbers remain the weak spot. Listen before you ship anything a person will act on, and say when the speech is synthetic.
